title: A Hybrid PINNs-FNO Approach for Advanced Option Pricing Models
content: Accurate option pricing remains a cornerstone of quantitative finance, where capturing the intricate dynamics of financial markets poses a persistent challenge. Traditional approaches, like the Black-Scholes framework, suffer from restrictive assumptions, while emerging deep learning techniques often prioritize either physical consistency or data-driven flexibility, rarely achieving both. This study proposes a novel hybrid framework that combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) to overcome these limitations. By leveraging the complementary strengths of PINNs for embedding the governing equations of the Black-Scholes model and FNOs for capturing complex, global relationships, the hybrid model achieves remarkable accuracy and robustness. Our methodology is validated on synthetic datasets representing local volatility surfaces, demonstrating significant performance improvements. The hybrid approach outperforms standalone PINNs and FNOs across key metrics, achieving a Mean Squared Error (MSE) reduction of up to 50% and enhanced generalization capabilities. Furthermore, extensive visualizations confirm the model’s ability to reconcile mathematical consistency with the adaptability required for real-world applications. This work not only advances the state-of-the-art in option pricing but also establishes a scalable and extensible framework applicable to broader domains governed by partial differential equations. By bridging the gap between theoretical finance and modern machine learning, the proposed approach opens new horizons for practical applications in risk management, hedging strategies, and derivative pricing.
